Ancient Troy History for Sleep 🌙

About 1 hour 54 min · Released Fri 6 Nov 2026 · narrated slowly for sleep

Watch on YouTube Listen on YouTube Music

Ancient Troy history for sleep: around 1280 BCE, Muwattalli II sealed a treaty with Alaksandu of Wilusa, which most historians think was Troy.

Tonight I walk the sloping walls of a hill of ten cities and read the clay letters that name Wilusa. Most historians think Wilusa was Troy, the city Homer called Ilios. The tablets were found far to the east, in the Hittite capital of Hattusa, recording a treaty around 1280 BCE between Muwattalli II and Alaksandu. I follow the diggers who put the layers in order, and where the records fall quiet, I simply say so.

🌙 No mid-video ads, nothing to wake you.

About this sleep story

About 1 hour 54 min, narrated slowly for sleep, with no ad breaks. Made as history to fall asleep to: it's fine to drift off partway, and the chapters below let you find your place again.

The Late Bronze Age city of Troy VI to VIIa (about 1750 to 1180 BCE), read beside the Hittite letters that name Wilusa; then Greek and Roman Ilion; then the people who dug the hill.

Sources

Researched and written for this channel from these sources. Where historians disagree, the narration says so.

  • G. Beckman, Hittite Diplomatic Texts (2nd ed. 1999) no. 13 (CTH 76), via British Museum record 108569
  • British Museum, tablet 108569, fragment of the Alaksandu treaty, from Boğazköy https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/W_1913-1011-22
  • UNESCO World Heritage List no. 849, Archaeological Site of Troy https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/849/
  • J. B. Rutter, Aegean Prehistoric Archaeology, Lesson 23: Troy VI, Dartmouth College https://sites.dartmouth.edu/aegean-prehistory/lessons/lesson-23-narrative/
  • J. B. Rutter, Aegean Prehistoric Archaeology, Lesson 27: Troy VII and the historicity of the Trojan War, Dartmouth College https://sites.dartmouth.edu/aegean-prehistory/lessons/lesson-27-narrative/
  • D. F. Easton, J. D. Hawkins, A. G. Sherratt, E. S. Sherratt, 'Troy in recent perspective', Anatolian Studies 52 (2002) (PDF text read 31 Oct 2026)
  • Herodotus, Histories 7.43, tr. A. D. Godley (Perseus)
  • Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander 1.11-12, tr. E. J. Chinnock (Wikisource)
  • J. D. Hawkins and D. F. Easton, 'A Hieroglyphic Seal from Troia', Studia Troica 6 (1996)
